question_stem:
A battery of electromotive force (e.m.f.) $E$ and internal resistance $r$ is connected to a variable resistor of resistance $R$, as shown in Fig. 6.1.

{{figure:figure_6_1}}

Fig. 6.1

The current in the circuit is $I$ and the potential difference across the variable resistor is $V$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in terms of energy, why $V$ is less than $E$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.part_stem:
The resistance $R$ of the variable resistor is varied. The variation with $I$ of $V$ is shown in Fig. 6.2.

{{figure:figure_6_2}}

Fig. 6.2

Use Fig. 6.2 to:
parts.text: explain how it may be deduced that the e.m.f. of the battery is $2.8\text{ V}$

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.part_stem: The battery stores $9.2\text{ kJ}$ of energy. The variable resistor is adjusted so that $V = 2.1\text{ V}$. Use Fig. 6.2 to:

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: calculate the number of conduction electrons moving through the battery in a time of $1.0\text{ s}$

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text: determine the time taken for the energy in the battery to become equal to $1.6\text{ kJ}$. (Assume that the e.m.f. of the battery and the current in the battery remain constant.)
